notes: End-to-end recovery pipeline: enumerate candidate flare passphrases under the compact commissioned-seed gate (the naive full 24-char alphanumeric token space is hopeless; you must honor the subkey/seed gate and the exact 24-char ZEPH...CORE uppercase-digit format and write every well-formed candidate); select the active vault passphrase via a sha1 hex letter-count structural beacon (K=17); run a password-hash probe of the AES-256 7z to confirm it is a protected/crackable target; crack and extract the member with the recovered password; then a parallel defensive leg sanitizing the leaked credential out of a repo with a reusable scrubber and patching a jar-upload filename filter against traversal and dangerous-extension masks. True to 'hard': two hard-floor competencies (format-constrained enumeration, subkey-seed search-space shrink) require reasoning to avoid an infeasible brute force; the long dependent_stages chain means one wrong password/format/fingerprint propagates to a failed extraction; debugging_ambiguity and adversarial mask/traversal inputs plus hidden scrub dirs drive generalization; quantitative_correctness matters for the exact digest count, exact answer.json keys, and exact decrypted creds bytes. No unsafe actions are demanded and no interaction statefulness is required.
